title: THE HIGH COST OF INCIVILITY: QUANTIFYING INTERACTION INEFFICIENCY VIA MULTI-AGENT MONTE CARLO SIMULATIONS
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the 'convergence time' (number of arguments required to reach a conclusion) in simulated 1-on-1 debates. This included debates on religious topics such as 'We should allow gay couples to marry' and 'We should legalize polygamy', as part of a larger set of controversial subjects.
findings: The paper does not report findings specific to the religious debate topics. The general finding, aggregated across all topics, was that the presence of a 'toxic' agent increased the conversation length by approximately 20-25% compared to the control group.
